entry.label: Do Bees Pee?
entry.description: A 2026 children's book using questions about animal waste to introduce ecological cycles, reuse and circular-economy thinking.
entry.canonical_definition: A 2026 children's book using questions about animal waste to introduce ecological cycles, reuse and circular-economy thinking.

profile.summary: Do Bees Pee? uses questions about animal waste and ecological reuse to introduce closed-loop processes and circular-economy thinking.
profile.canonical_definition: Do Bees Pee? uses questions about animal waste and ecological reuse to introduce closed-loop processes and circular-economy thinking.
profile.why_it_matters: It extends Booth Sweeney's systems-literacy work into the material cycles through which one organism's output becomes another process's resource.
key_distinctions: The June 2026 publication fact and framing are established by the author's current publication notice.
common_misreadings: A closed loop is a useful model, not a claim that material systems have no losses or externalities.
open_checks: Add the publisher record and independent reviews after publication where available.

connections.scope_conditions: The author explicitly frames the book as an introduction to sustainability and circular-economy thinking.
